name: RDGL (Roland DG Language)
_comment: RDGL is HPGL with a Roland-specific init sequence and an explicit reset on eject. The move and draw command forms are identical to HPGL (PU;PA%.0f,%.0f; and PD%.0f,%.0f;), so this profile uses the hpgl protocol. The init header is '/e/50A/e/50BBP5,1;!ST1;PA;PU;'. Where a vendor definition substitutes its own speed and force words into the header, this profile instead this profile keeps the static init prefix in 'header' and lets setup_commands append the force/speed words afterwards. The trailing 'PU;' from the vendor header is dropped for the same reason: setup_commands may itself emit a pen-up, and a duplicate PU; is harmless but unnecessary.
_footer_comment: FD=!PG; is the eject/finish command. Some vendor definitions also give a long PJL reset sequence ('PU;(FEED)PU;PA0,0;/e/5-12345X@PJL RESET @PJL ENTER LANGUAGE=RESET'). That sequence resets the printer language and is only meaningful on a device that speaks PJL; on a plain cutter it can leave the port in a state the next job cannot recover from. This profile sends the safe eject (!PG;) and leaves the PJL reset to the operator.
_tool_comment: RDGL drives Roland plotters and cutters. A drag knife needs corner compensation; a pen does not. 0.25 mm suits a 45 degree blade.
